bulk_sample.description:
Each sample is 4 bytes. Bulk data: [4-byte u32le timestamp] + [N × 4-byte sample records].
Each sample record: byte[0]=type prefix, byte[1..3] encoded temp/humidity value.
Stop token: 0xFFFFFFFF marks end of valid data.
TLV-style: type_prefix byte determines interpretation (65=standard reading).

device.name: SensorPush HT1 / HTP.xw
device.notes:
Protocol documented via community reverse engineering.
Primary sources: sensorpush-bleak (cryptomcgrath, 5★) and sensorpush-ble (Bluetooth-Devices).
Two hardware generations: HT1 (V1, thermometer only) and HTP.xw (V2, thermometer + hygrometer).
TI CC2540/CC2541 BLE SoC. Uses OAD (Over-the-Air Download) firmware update service.
Temperature/humidity accessed via write-then-read pattern: write 4-byte trigger, 110ms delay, then read.
History data retrieved in bulk notification chunks with 4-byte timestamp header.
Device reports battery voltage + raw temperature sensor in Battery Info characteristic.
Uses SensorPush BLE Advertisement Detection: name/address prefix check plus UUID slicing.

credentials.notes: BLE-only; no WiFi passphrase crosses the link. The connection is unauthenticated, so readings and logged history are available to anyone in range.

factory_reset.effect: Not established. The sensor holds logged history that a reset would clear, but neither community implementation documents a reset command, and the device exposes a TI OAD firmware-update service on adjacent handles — guessing at opcodes near that is how a sensor ends up in bootloader mode. Removing the battery is the only safe state change.

methods.description: Connect over GATT and read temperature and humidity with the write-then-read pattern: write the 4-byte trigger, wait ~110 ms, then read the result.

steps.action: Insert the battery; the sensor advertises continuously from power-on.
Scan for the SensorPush name/address prefix and match the primary service UUID to identify the generation — ...090aa9 for HT1, ...090ab0 for HTP.xw.
Connect over GATT. No pairing is requested.
Write the 4-byte trigger to the measurement characteristic, wait 110 ms, then read it back.
steps.expect: A current temperature (and humidity, on HTP.xw) reading.

setup.notes:
Nothing is provisioned. The sensor advertises continuously and serves readings to any client that connects; there is no pairing, bonding or account. The SensorPush app's cloud gateway is a separate product, not a prerequisite for reading the sensor.
Which generation you have decides the service UUID — HT1 (V1) ends ...090aa9, HTP.xw (V2) ends ...090ab0 — so detection must check both.
Confidence is medium: the flow comes from two independent community implementations (sensorpush-bleak, sensorpush-ble) rather than from a run against hardware here.

rejoin.notes: The sensor joins no network. Any client may connect once the previous one disconnects.

services.notes: V2/HTP.xw (temperature + humidity) exposes the counterpart service ef090000-11d6-42ba-93b8-9dd7ec090ab0. Its characteristic UUIDs follow the same …ab0 base but were not individually recovered.
